# Upgrading

<!-- Generated by scripts/release.mjs from releases.json and the git history: do not edit. -->

Before installing a new version, apply the actions of every version after the one you run, up to the one you install, oldest first. A **mandatory stop** must be installed and started once before you upgrade past it. Versions not listed here need no manual action.

A release candidate counts as its final version: it needs the same actions, so upgrading from X.Y.Z-rc.N to X.Y.Z needs none.

From a copy of the repository, `node scripts/upgrade-path.mjs <from> <to>` lists the actions and stops of your upgrade.

## 0.11.0

- Only if your own scripts call the Cellar API: send `GET /api/admin/download-backup?filename=` instead of `?file=`, which now answers `422`. Read what a `PUT` saved instead of `{ success: true }` from `PUT /api/settings`, `/api/admin/backup-settings`, `/api/admin/barcode-settings` (with its `conflictInfo`), `/api/admin/upgrade-actions` and `/api/admin/images` (the image as `GET /api/admin/images` lists it, its wines in `wines`), and expect `204` without a body from `PUT /api/access-code`. Read the name of the backup made before a wipe in `backup` of `POST /api/admin/wipe-database`, instead of `backups.database` (its `size` is gone). Expect `204` without a body from `DELETE /api/admin/wine-definitions/{id}` and `DELETE /api/admin/images`, and `201` from `POST /api/admin/upload-image` and `POST /api/admin/import-images-zip`. No longer expect `message` from `POST /api/bottles` nor `success` from `POST /api/upload/image`. Send a purchase price and a current value of 0 or more to `POST` and `PATCH /api/bottles`, which answer `422` to a negative one. Expect `404` from `DELETE /api/admin/wine-bottles/{id}` for a bottle that does not exist, and from `GET /api/wines/{id}/locations` for a wine that does not exist. Read the wine of `GET /api/bottles/non-consumed` in `definition` instead of `wineDefinition`, and the location of `GET /api/definitions/{id}` in `appellation` only, as `appellations`, `regions` and `countries` are gone. Handle `409 barcode_generation_off` from `GET /api/admin/next-barcode` while automatic barcodes are off, instead of `200` with an empty `barcode`. Read each wine of `GET /api/wines` as `{ "definition", "bottles" }`, as the fields of its first bottle are no longer at the top level, a wine without bottles no longer has the id `def-<wine id>`, and each bottle no longer repeats its wine in `definition`. `docs/API.md` describes every answer.

## 0.9.0

- Scripts that call `PUT /api/bottles/{id}` must switch to `PATCH` and send only the fields to change.

## 0.8.0

- Only if your own scripts call the Cellar API: `PUT /api/storage-containers/{id}` must list every case of the container, in order, as a case left out is now deleted.

## 0.7.0

- Only if your own scripts call the Cellar API: read an error from `error.code` and `error.message`, as errors are no longer a plain `error` text; send ids, not names, for the type, color, classification, format and origin of wines and bottles; call `/api/<table>` instead of `/api/admin/<table>` for wine types, colors, formats and classifications, origins, countries, regions and appellations, and send `name` for wine types and colors; read the saved entry from a PUT instead of `{ success: true }`; and use `/api/definitions` instead of `/api/wines` to create or change a wine.

## 0.5.0

- Only if you run Cellar from source instead of Docker, or if your container overrides the image's start command (for example `command: node build` in a compose file or a NAS template): start the built app with `node server.js` instead of `node build`, with `ORIGIN` set as before, for example `ORIGIN=http://localhost:3000 node server.js`. SvelteKit 3 no longer reads `ORIGIN` in `node build`, so every save, import, upload or delete would fail with 403. Other Docker users have nothing to do: the image starts this way and keeps reading `ORIGIN` from the same `.env` file.

## 0.4.0

- Only if you printed barcode labels before 0.4.0. Labels made from the barcode **CSV export** carry 13-character codes that match no bottle: print them again. Labels from the **PDF** do not scan on many label templates, because their barcode was cut off at its right end: scan one label from each PDF sheet you printed, and print again every sheet whose labels do not scan. Print the new labels from the PDF or from a new CSV export. The codes stored on your bottles do not change, so a reprinted label matches the same bottle.

## 0.3.0

- Only if you run Cellar from source instead of Docker: use Node 24 and pnpm 10. `pnpm install` now refuses other Node versions, and runs the exact pnpm version set by `packageManager` in `package.json`. `package-lock.json` is gone, so `npm install` is no longer supported. Docker users have nothing to do.

## 0.2.0

- Set `ORIGIN` to the exact URL you open Cellar with: scheme, host and port, no trailing slash (for example `ORIGIN=http://192.168.1.20:3005`). With the repository's `docker-compose.yml`, take the new version of the file, copy `.env.example` to `.env` next to it and fill in `ORIGIN`: `docker compose` refuses to start without it. With your own compose file or `docker run`, add the variable to the container's environment. If `ORIGIN` is missing or does not match the URL in the browser, pages load but every save, import, upload or delete fails with 403. Behind a reverse proxy that serves several hostnames, set `PROTOCOL_HEADER` and `HOST_HEADER` instead: see [Application URL (ORIGIN)](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#application-url-origin).
- Cellar now runs as an unprivileged user (uid 1000) instead of root, so the data written by earlier versions, which belongs to root, must be given to that user before you start the new version. With the repository's `docker-compose.yml`, run `sudo chown -R 1000:1000 docker-data` next to it. With any other setup (other folders, named volumes, or no `sudo` on the host), run this command with the folders or volumes your container mounts as `-v` sources, and drop the `-v` of any you do not mount: `docker run --rm -v <data>:/app/data -v <uploads>:/app/static/uploads -v <csv-imports>:/app/csv-imports alpine chown -R 1000:1000 /app/data /app/static/uploads /app/csv-imports`. To run Cellar as another account instead, for example the one that owns your NAS shares (find its numbers with `id <account>`, often `1026:100` on Synology or `99:100` on Unraid), add `user: "1026:100"` to the service and use `1026:100` in place of `1000:1000` in these commands. If you skip this step, the container stops right after starting, and its log names the folders and files it cannot write to and how to fix them: see [Data ownership](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#data-ownership).
- If automatic backups use the **External Cron Job** mode, the cron job that runs `curl -X POST …/api/admin/auto-backup` now fails and no backup is made: the admin API requires a login session. In Cellar, open Admin, then the automatic backup settings, and set **Backup Mode** to **Internal Scheduler**; on a version before 0.6.0, restart the container afterwards, as saving the settings did not start the scheduler yet. From 0.6.0 on, you can instead keep the External Cron Job mode, with a token that Cellar generates: see [Automatic backups](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#automatic-backups).
- If your access code was still the default `1234`, it is removed when Cellar starts. To choose a new one, open Cellar and enter the setup token that the server prints in the container logs (`docker compose logs cellar`). A code you had chosen keeps working. See [Access code](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#access-code).
- Behind a reverse proxy, set `ADDRESS_HEADER` (and `XFF_DEPTH`) so that wrong access codes are counted per client: otherwise every request seems to come from the proxy, and one client's wrong codes block everyone. See [Client addresses behind a reverse proxy](https://github.com/Lulu300/cellar/blob/main/README-Docker.md#client-addresses-behind-a-reverse-proxy).
- Backups made before 0.2.0 hold the access code in clear. Delete the copies you no longer need, or change the code if copies are kept elsewhere.
